In `Q4VoltaDp4aSchedule` (defined in `src/ops/linear/q4/q4_volta_dp4a_gemm.cuh`):

- **`kTileN = 64`** — output rows per CTA (the lane axis, stride 32)
- **`kTileT = 128`** — tokens per CTA (the warp axis, stride `kNWarps` = 8)

**`kStrideW = 17`** (i.e. `kWordsK + 1` = 16 + 1).

It is one more than the 16 int32 words that make up a group-row so that the stride is **odd**, which guarantees that the 32 lanes reading 32 different weight rows in the same column hit 32 distinct shared-memory banks (17 is coprime to 32), eliminating the bank conflicts an even stride like 16 would cause.

The constant is **`kQ4Dp4aMinT`** and its value is **128**.

It is defined in `q4_launch.h` with the comment explaining that dp4a's 128-token tile wants a wide T, so MTP verify widths (T≤8) and small prefill chunks stay on the fp16 mma route, while real prefill (chunk 2048) is well above the threshold.

Per 64-element group:

- **`kCodeBytesPerGroup = 32`** — the low-nibble plane (4 bits per weight × 64 weights / 2 per byte)
- **`kHighBytesPerGroup = 8`** — the high-bit plane (1 bit per weight × 64 weights / 8 per byte)

The expression is:

```
(high[K/8] >> (K % 8)) & 1
```

This is stated verbatim in the file's header comment: *"The high bit for weight K is (high[K/8] >> (K%8)) & 1."*

Each of the 8 bytes in the high plane holds 8 high bits (one per weight), so byte `K/8` covers weights `8·(K/8) … 8·(K/8)+7`, and bit position `K%8` within that byte is weight K's top bit. The kernel's inner loop implements the same logic in a vectorised form (extracting 4 bits at a time via `(hbyte >> (4*(word&1))) & 0xf`), but it reduces to this per-weight expression.

The second argument to `__launch_bounds__` is the **minimum number of blocks the compiler must fit per SM**. Setting it to 2 caps the per-thread register allocation at 65536 / (256 × 2) = **128 registers**, which is the budget that lets two 256-thread blocks (16 warps, 25% occupancy) co-reside on a V100 SM.

The concrete problem: the Q5 5-bit decode (low nibble + high-bit extraction + XOR/shift to form the signed value in [−16, 15]) naturally wants more live registers than the Q4 4-bit decode. Without the bound, the compiler allocates enough registers for that wider decode, pushing the count above 128 per thread and dropping the kernel to **1 block per SM (8 warps, 12.5% occupancy)**. The code comment states this directly:

> *"the extra 5-bit-decode registers were pinning the kernel to 1 block/SM (12.5% occupancy) vs the Q4 sibling's 2 blocks."*

Forcing the second argument to 2 tells the compiler it must stay within 128 registers, so it spills or restructures the decode to fit. The result is 2 blocks/SM, matching the Q4 sibling's occupancy, which is what the kernel needs to keep enough warps in flight to hide the DRAM latency of the scattered per-lane weight-row streams in the main loop.

```cpp
} else if (attn_q4_dp4a_prefill_enabled() && t >= kQ4Dp4aMinT &&
           q4_volta_dp4a_supported(qk_out.ne[0], k, t)) {
```

This is the third branch in the `if / else if` chain inside the first scoped block of `attn_input_proj_graph_shard_launch`. It requires all three conditions to hold:

1. `attn_q4_dp4a_prefill_enabled()` — the `NINFER_NO_DP4A` environment variable is not set to `"1"` (the A/B toggle read once at first call).
2. `t >= kQ4Dp4aMinT` — the token width is at least 128, so the 128-token dp4a tile is well-utilised.
3. `q4_volta_dp4a_supported(qk_out.ne[0], k, t)` — the shape is structurally valid (positive dimensions, `k` a multiple of the 64-element group).

It passes **`add_residual = false`**.

The MLP down projection produces a plain (non-residual) partial `W@x` that is later summed with the residual by a separate `residual_add_two` op, so there is no pre-existing residual to fold into the store — the kernel writes its result fresh rather than reading-adding-writing `out` in place.

At the prefill chunk width the code targets (T = 2048), every GEMM in the three components resolves as follows:

## dp4a route (int8 `__dp4a`, compute-bound)

| GEMM | Weight format | Why dp4a |
|---|---|---|
| MLP gate/up | Q4 | T = 2048 ≥ `kQ4Dp4aMinT` (128); the `q4_volta_dp4a_supported` guard passes for the shard shapes |
| MLP down | Q5 | Same threshold; `launch_q5_volta_dp4a` called with `add_residual = false` |
| Attention input – query_key | Q4 | Same threshold in `attn_input_proj_graph_shard_launch` |
| Attention input – gate_value | Q5 | Same threshold; `launch_q5_volta_dp4a` with `add_residual = false` |

All four hit their dp4a branch before the fp16-mma branch is ever evaluated, because the dp4a `else-if` precedes the mma `else-if` in each dispatch chain.

## fp16 mma route (tensor cores, FP16 operands)

| GEMM | Weight format | Why fp16 mma (CUTLASS) |
|---|---|---|
| GDN input – qk | Q4 | T = 2048 is **above** `kVoltaMmaMaxCols` (64), so `gdn_uses_volta_mma` returns false and the plan stays `CutlassSm70TensorCore` |
| GDN input – value | Q5 | Same reason; the CUTLASS path dequants the value rows of `value_z_weight` to global FP16 |
| GDN input – z | Q5 | Same reason; pointer offset into the same dequant buffer |

The GDN input projection is the only component that does **not** take the dp4a route at prefill width. Its fused-kernel band (`kVoltaMmaMinCols` = 12 through `kVoltaMmaMaxCols` = 64) is designed for the mid-range token widths where the fused in-shared-memory dequant amortises well. At T = 2048 the plan falls through to `CutlassSm70TensorCore`, which materialises both parent weights (Q4 qk and Q5 value_z) into global FP16 scratch and runs three CUTLASS Sm70 `mma.sync.m8n8k4` GEMMs. The dp4a check lives *inside* the `VoltaMmaFused` execute path, which is never reached at this width, so the GDN GEMMs remain on the FP16 tensor-core route.
